title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: World Court issues first genocide verdict
preheader: The ICJ ruled Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention in 2017 attacks on Rohingya.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Friday, November 20, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 7 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: ICJ finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
stories.why_important: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar broke the Genocide Convention in its 2017 attacks on Rohingya Muslims. This is the first time the court has found a state at fault for genocide. The ruling could shape South Africa's genocide case against Israel.
stories.what_overlooked: The ruling does not order payments yet, but a separate phase will decide what Myanmar owes. The Security Council decides how to enforce the ruling.
stories.prediction: Myanmar's junta will likely reject the ruling within days. The UN Security Council may then meet on how to enforce it.

stories.story_title: COP31 draft drops call to phase out fossil fuels
stories.why_important: At the COP31 climate summit, negotiators removed a call to end fossil fuels faster. They took it out of a revised draft deal. Countries and activists objected loudly, saying the summit is weakening its core promise, and a final deal is expected on Friday.
stories.what_overlooked: The draft still mentions a broad shift in energy. But it no longer names coal, oil and gas, which scientists call the main causes of warming.
stories.prediction: A full session on Friday will either adopt the weakened text or send it back. The EU and exposed countries may block a final deal.

stories.story_title: White House fires cyber chief after widespread tech outages
stories.why_important: President Trump removed National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross after a week of outages that disrupted air travel, banking and classified messages. The White House named a Defense Department official to the post on a temporary basis. Lawmakers are demanding answers about the outages that disrupted air travel and banking.
stories.what_overlooked: The outages hit Microsoft users worldwide and halted US air travel. The government has not published a timeline of what failed.
stories.prediction: Senate committees may call Cairncross or the temporary director to testify. They may also demand a public timeline of the outages.

quick_hits.text: Haiti's police killed at least 34 suspected gang members in an operation to retake the Martissant corridor in Port-au-Prince.
A Pentagon official told the Senate the US war on Iran has cost $48.3 billion, excluding damage to US bases.
Saudi Arabia's coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at the kingdom's southern region.
Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman blamed India for escalating violence as Sheikh Hasina's supporters vandalized the ruling party office.
The US, China and Russia signed a 'peace declaration' after their summit, pledging nuclear risk talks but no arms control.
Trump left China without meeting Kim Jong-un, saying a meeting could still happen at some point.
Pew Research projects Muslims will outnumber Christians by 2035, with Islam becoming the world's largest religion.
